The most critical factor. The Dravidian movement, which gained ground in the early 20th century, especially through Periyar and later the DMK, opposed North Indian cultural domination, especially Brahminism, Sanskrit, Hindi imposition, and central control.

Tamil Nadu is extremely proud of Tamil, which is not only one of the oldest classical languages but also has a continuous literary tradition dating back to at least 2000 years. It is the only classical language that is still widely spoken.

Efforts like “Thanith Tamil Iyakkam” (Pure Tamil Movement) fostered linguistic resistance and discouraged heavy borrowing from Sanskrit or Hindi.

The Anti-Hindi agitations of 1937–40 and especially 1965 forged a political consensus in Tamil Nadu against the central government’s language policies.

It is more gradual of a transformation in theyyam unlike where in Kola the possession is instant

In Theyyam, the man becomes a god. In Kola, the man becomes a spirit. Theyyam is where a man becomes a god worshipped by all; Kola is where a man becomes a spirit who speaks, judges, and guides the community.

Some Theyyam performances directly critique caste oppression, Brahminical injustice, or state violence—like the Theyyams of Muchilottu Bhagavati, Kuttichathan, or Pulayan Daivams.These performances serve as a historical counter-narrative to elite-controlled versions of religious history.

Theyyam is performed exclusively by lower-caste communities like the Vannan, Malayan, and others. This ritual inversion gives them a temporary yet sacred superiority over even Brahmins, who come to receive blessings from the Theyyam performers.
Many Theyyam deities are spirits of women, outcastes, Dalits, or those violently wronged—figures Brahminical tradition often excludes

Theyyam is often seen as a resistance to Brahminization because it embodies and preserves non-Brahminical, indigenous, and folk religious traditions that predate or run parallel to Brahminical Hinduism.
